seoTitle: How to Earn Money With Hostinger's Referral Program
metaDescription: Hostinger's referral program pays 20% of a referred customer's first purchase, not a flat fee per plan. Here's where the link lives and how the payout rules work.
intro: Hostinger runs its referral program right inside the account dashboard, so anyone who already hosts a site with them can start earning without installing anything or applying to a separate affiliate network. The reward is a percentage of what the person you refer spends on their first purchase, and because Hostinger sells everything from shared hosting to VPS and business email, the commission on a single referral can add up. This guide shows where the referral tool lives in the dashboard, how the reward gets triggered, and which plans qualify from how short a term.
prerequisites: An existing Hostinger account — the referral tool is already built into the dashboard, with no separate application

steps.heading: Find the referral button in your dashboard
steps.body: Once you're logged in, look at the top navigation bar next to the search box for a gift-icon button labeled "Refer & earn." It's visible from every page of the dashboard, including Home, Websites, Domains and Horizons, so there's no digging through settings menus. If you're building with Hostinger's AI Builder, the same tool is also reachable from the editor's own menu. Clicking it opens the referral hub where your unique link and sharing options live.

image.caption: The Hostinger dashboard with the "Refer & earn up to 200 USD" button sitting in the top bar, next to the account search.

steps.heading: Understand what has to happen before you're paid
steps.body: The referral hub lays out four steps: you send an invite, they make a purchase, they stay active for at least 45 days without requesting a refund, and only then does the commission unlock. A friend who signs up and cancels within that window generates nothing, so referring people who genuinely intend to use hosting matters more than raw invite volume. Once earnings clear that window, Hostinger sends them out by PayPal, wire transfer, or Hostinger Balance, not only the first two; balance is instant account credit you can put toward your own services.

image.caption: The "How do referrals work?" panel, showing the four-step path from invite to payout and the 45-day activity requirement.

steps.heading: Know it's a percentage, not a fixed fee per plan
steps.body: The commission is 20% of whatever the referred customer pays on their first purchase, not a flat dollar figure that happens to be bigger for pricier plans. The breakdown table further down the referral hub shows a different payout for each hosting tier for exactly that reason: 20% of a higher-priced plan is a bigger number, not a different rate. Renewals and upgrades after that first purchase don't generate anything further for a standard referral participant; that ongoing cut is reserved for Hostinger's separate, invite-only Partner tier.

image.caption: The commission breakdown table, listing each hosting plan's price alongside the referral commission it pays out.

steps.heading: Share your link where it will convert
steps.body: A referral link buried in one old tweet won't do much. If you run a blog or a YouTube channel, a short, honest mention in content about building a website converts better than a bare link in a bio, since it gives the viewer a reason to switch hosts. Friends or coworkers who've mentioned wanting a website, or moving off a slower host, are worth a direct message with your link instead of a mass post.

steps.heading: Track sign-ups and stay within the terms
steps.body: The referral hub doubles as a tracking dashboard, showing which invites converted and where each one sits in the 45-day window before it counts toward a payout. Read the linked Terms of Service once: referral programs commonly restrict things like referring yourself with a second account, or bidding on the word "Hostinger" in paid ads, and violating those terms can get commissions clawed back or the account suspended.

troubleshooting.problem: A referral signed up and canceled a few weeks later, and you got nothing
troubleshooting.cause: Commission only unlocks after the referred customer stays active for 45 days without a refund.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the referral hub's status column to see where each invite sits in that 45-day window before counting it as earned.

troubleshooting.problem: A referral bought Shared Hosting on a short plan and it didn't count
troubleshooting.cause: Shared Hosting and AI Builder plans only qualify for commission on subscriptions of 12 months or longer; the shorter terms are excluded.
troubleshooting.fix: Point referrals choosing Shared Hosting or an AI Builder plan toward a 12-month term, or toward a different product line (VPS, Cloud Hosting, email) that qualifies from 1 month.

troubleshooting.cause: Each payout method has its own minimum: $50 for PayPal, $200 for wire transfer, $30 for Hostinger Balance.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to Hostinger Balance for the lowest threshold, or wait for more referrals to clear before requesting PayPal or wire.

faq.question: How much can I earn per referral with Hostinger?
faq.answer: 20% of whatever the referred customer pays on their first purchase. Higher-priced plans pay more in dollars for the same reason a bigger receipt produces a bigger 20% of it, not because the rate itself changes.

faq.question: Do I earn anything when a referral renews or upgrades?
faq.answer: Not as a standard referral participant; the reward is on the first purchase only. Recurring commission on renewals is limited to Hostinger's separate, invite-only Partner program.

faq.question: Is $200 a guaranteed amount?
faq.answer: No. It reflects the upper end of what's possible on higher-tier plans, not a guaranteed payout for every sign-up.

faq.question: When does a referral commission get paid?
faq.answer: Only after the referred customer completes a purchase and stays active on it for at least 45 days without a refund. Payout requests are also subject to a minimum: $50 for PayPal, $200 for wire, $30 for Hostinger Balance.

faq.question: Does every plan qualify from just one month?
faq.answer: No. Shared Hosting and AI Builder plans need a 12-month or longer term to count; other products like VPS, Cloud Hosting and Business Email qualify from a 1-month term.

faq.question: Where do I find my referral link?
faq.answer: Click the "Refer & earn" button in the top navigation bar of your Hostinger dashboard, or the same tool inside the AI Builder editor, then copy the link for the plan you want to recommend.
